**The Impact You'll Make

**As our Senior Coordinator, Product Data Management (PDM), you'll play a key role in ensuring that our product data is accurate, consistent and accessible across our global engineering organization.

You'll be part of the PL40 Engineering organization and work closely with our Global Product Data Management team, connecting colleagues, systems and processes across different functions and locations. From maintaining critical product information to supporting new product development and global system implementations, your work will help teams make better decisions and operate more efficiently.

Your impact? You'll go beyond managing data — you'll help improve how we work with it. By driving standardization, identifying opportunities for automation and coordinating improvements across sites, you'll contribute to more reliable processes, smoother project execution and better data quality throughout Danfoss.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**In this role, you will:

• Own and maintain high-quality product master data, including material masters, Bills of Materials (BOMs), classifications, technical documentation and product labels, ensuring accuracy and consistency across systems.

• Support colleagues and coordinate PDM activities across functions and locations, providing guidance on systems, preparing risk assessments, analyzing data in Excel and ensuring timely resolution of data-related issues.

• Drive local and global process improvements, identifying opportunities for standardization, optimization and automation while collaborating with the Global PDM team and service excellence centers.

• Contribute to key business and system projects, including OneERP implementation, PLM-related initiatives and Product Data Management improvements, ensuring effective implementation at the local site.

• Coordinate product data activities within New Product Development (NPD) projects, working closely with the Global NPD Coordinator, engineering teams and international stakeholders to ensure accurate and timely product data availability.

**What We're Looking For

**

• A technical or administrative educational background, combined with at least 3–5 years of experience in Product Data Management, master data or a similar area.

• Strong SAP and Microsoft Excel skills, with practical experience managing complex product data; familiarity with Siemens Teamcenter or other PLM systems would be a valuable advantage.

• A structured, detail-oriented and quality-focused approach, with a strong commitment to data accuracy, consistency and a zero-defect mindset.

• A proactive, solution-oriented mindset with the ability to take ownership, prioritize tasks, drive improvements and deliver results in a dynamic environment.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, fluency in written and spoken English, and the confidence to work effectively with stakeholders across different functions and international locations.

**What You'll Get From Us

**

• A role with real ownership and impact, where your work directly supports product development, engineering operations and the quality of critical business data.

• The opportunity to contribute to global transformation initiatives, including OneERP implementation, process standardization and improvements to Product Data Management systems.

• International collaboration with our Global PDM team in Denmark, engineering colleagues and stakeholders across multiple Danfoss locations.

• The chance to develop your expertise in SAP, PLM systems, master data governance and process optimization, while taking an active role in improving the way we work.

• A supportive and collaborative engineering environment where your ideas are valued, continuous improvement is encouraged and you can build your professional network within a global organization.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

Whether you have a couple of years of experience or a few more, we would like to see your application.

**What's in it for you?

**

• Build on a system with real scale behind it. The event system spans 8 domains, exposes 20+ event types as webhooks, and powers 10 configurable alert types for our end users - currently ~20k active configurations triggering ~200k events every weekday. • Nice to have: Flink and stateful processing (or the willingness to learn it, since it is widely used here), relational databases, and Grafana and Prometheus, our “bread and butter”.

You embrace AI as part of how you engineer. From prototyping through to production, you use AI tools as an integrated part of your workflow, not as a shortcut but as a force multiplier. That said, this isn't the main thing we're hiring for: curiosity and a willingness to use it well matter more than deep prior experience.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) Religious Education, Legal Consciousness and Social Cohesion in Post-Imperial Islamic Societies
jobs.description:
The Department of Law at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded three-year PhD position within the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network MINARET – Islamic Legal Cultures in Post-Imperial Contexts. Employment is expected to begin September 1, 2027, or by agreement.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences and employed at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark.

 

About the MINARET Doctoral Network

MINARET is an international doctoral network funded through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA). The network investigates how Islamic legal cultures shape governance, citizenship, institutions and everyday legal practices across post-imperial societies.

The programme brings together universities and non-academic partners across Europe, North Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia. Doctoral candidates will receive interdisciplinary training, international supervision and extensive mobility opportunities.

Further information about the network is available at MINARET website.

 

Project Description

This doctoral project examines how constitutional and legal frameworks governing religious education shape citizenship, legal consciousness and social cohesion in Indonesia and Morocco.

The project investigates how constitutional values, religious identities and civic norms are translated into educational practices and everyday experiences of citizenship. Particular attention is paid to how religious education influences democratic participation, social integration and perceptions of rights, duties and belonging.

The project contributes to research on legal consciousness, sociology of law, citizenship studies and comparative constitutionalism. Through comparative empirical research in Indonesia and Morocco, the doctoral candidate will analyse how educational institutions function as sites where legal norms, religious values and civic identities intersect.

The candidate is expected to develop an original research design within the overall framework of the project.

 

Host Institution

The position is based at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark, Denmark.

The Department of Law is part of the Faculty of Social Sciences and hosts a vibrant interdisciplinary environment within sociology of law, legal anthropology, human rights and comparative legal studies.

The successful candidate will become part of the department’s research environment as well as the international MINARET doctoral network.

More information about our PhD programme is available at the department’s website. On the website, you will also find the department’s qualifications criteria. The programme is provided by the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences who offer further information on their website.

 

Supervision

The doctoral candidate will be supervised by:

• 
Professor Ole Hammerslev (University of Southern Denmark) (principal supervisor)

• 
Co-supervisor from MINARET consortium

Additional mentoring and supervision will be provided through the MINARET network.

 

Fieldwork and Mobility

The project includes substantial international mobility.

The doctoral candidate is expected to conduct fieldwork in:

• 
Indonesia

• 
Morocco

 

In addition, the candidate will undertake two secondments within the MINARET network:

• 
one academic secondment at a partner university;

• 
one non-academic secondment with a relevant partner organisation.

 

Participation in network-wide training events, workshops, summer schools and conferences is mandatory.

 

Tasks and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

• 
conduct independent doctoral research within the project framework;

• 
participate actively in the MINARET doctoral network;

• 
undertake international fieldwork and secondments;

• 
complete PhD courses and training activities;

• 
contribute to the research environment at the Department of Law;

• 
participate in teaching and related activities in accordance with Danish PhD regulations.

 

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree (or equivalent) in law, sociology, political science, anthropology, religious studies, education, or a related social science discipline.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences, SDU, which you can learn more about on the PhD School’s website. 

Applicants must also meet requirements in accordance with the MSCA Doctoral Network:

• 
applicants must not already hold a doctoral degree;

• 
applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.

Excellent English language skills are required.

 

Desired Qualifications

Preference will be given to applicants with documented experience or interest in one or more of the following areas:

• 
sociology of law;

• 
legal consciousness;

• 
citizenship studies;

• 
religion and law;

• 
Islamic legal cultures;

• 
qualitative and comparative research methods;

• 
fieldwork-based research.

 

Knowledge of Arabic, Bahasa Indonesia, French or other relevant languages is an advantage but not a requirement.

 

Assessment Criteria

Applicants will be assessed on:

academic qualifications (please consult the guidelines for recognizing merit at the Department of Law);

jobs.description:
Do you want to work for some of the world’s leading audio brands? Become a part of the HARMAN team and get to work for JBL and Harman/Kardon.

You will join our new Acoustics Engineering Lab within Harman Consumer Audio, based in Kvistgaard, Denmark in the position of:

Engineer New Technology & Innovation - Acoustic Measurement & Evaluation

Introduction: A Career at HARMAN Lifestyle:

We’re a global, multi-disciplinary team that’s putting the innovative power of technology to work and transforming tomorrow. As a member of HARMAN Lifestyle, you connect consumers with the power of superior sound.

• Contribute your talents to high-end, esteemed brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, Mark Levinson and Revel.

• Unite your passion for audio innovation with high-tech product development.

• Create pitch-perfect, cutting-edge technology that elevates listening experience.

HARMAN’s engineers and designers are creative, purposeful and agile. As part of this team, you’ll combine your technical expertise with innovative ideas to help drive cutting-edge solutions in the consumer audio systems. Every day, you will push the boundaries of creative design, and HARMAN is committed to providing you with the opportunities, innovative technologies and resources to build a successful career.

What You’ll Be Part Of

The Consumer Audio New Technology & Innovation (NT&I) team is at the center of audio technology innovation, supporting the development of HARMAN's next-generation consumer audio products, including over-ear headphones, true wireless stereo (TWS) earbuds, and open wireless stereo (OWS) devices. The NT&I Denmark team is seeking a Senior Engineer, Acoustic Measurement & Evaluation, to lead the development, execution, and continuous improvement of acoustic measurement and subjective evaluation methodologies for consumer audio products.

The successful candidate will be responsible for objective acoustic characterization of loudspeakers, headphones, earbuds, and emerging audio devices, as well as the design and management of laboratory test environments and listening evaluation programs.

This role combines deep expertise in electroacoustic measurements, data analysis, listening science, and laboratory operations to ensure industry-leading audio performance across our product portfolio.

How You’ll Make An Impact:

• Technical Leadership: Provide technical leadership in acoustic measurement and evaluation, establishing best practices, and driving continuous improvement of measurement capabilities, tools, and processes.

• Acoustic Measurement & Characterization: Lead the objective acoustic characterization of speakers, headphones, earbuds, and emerging audio products, utilizing advanced measurement techniques to assess frequency response, distortion, directivity, sensitivity, noise performance, and sound pressure capabilities.

• Subjective Evaluation & Listening Science: Design and conduct subjective listening evaluations, including listener panel management, competitive benchmarking, and the development of scientifically robust methodologies for assessing sound quality and user experience.

• Data Analysis & Performance Insights: Analyse and interpret objective and subjective performance data, generating actionable insights and developing meaningful correlations between acoustic measurements and listener preferences.

• Measurement Methodology & Standards: Develop, validate, and maintain measurement methodologies and standards, ensuring acoustic evaluations are accurate, repeatable, and aligned across development teams and laboratories.

• Acoustic Laboratory Development: Design, establish, and maintain state-of-the-art acoustic test facilities, including listening rooms, anechoic and semi-anechoic environments, ear-simulator and HATS-based measurement systems, and automated test platforms.

• Collaboration: Provide acoustic measurement and evaluation support for internally developed technologies, algorithms, and proof-of-concept systems, and collaborate with cross-functional teams on product validation, troubleshooting, performance optimization, and deployment.

What Makes You A Strong Fit:

Education & Experience:

• M.S. or Ph.D. in Acoustics, Audio Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Physics, or a related field.

• At least 8 years of experience in acoustic measurement, audio product development, electroacoustic testing, or acoustic research.

• Demonstrated experience leading technical initiatives and driving improvements in measurement methodologies, laboratory capabilities, or audio evaluation processes.

Technical Skills:

• Strong expertise in objective acoustic measurement and characterization of speakers, headphones, earbuds, and related audio systems, including frequency response, distortion, directivity, sensitivity, noise, and SPL performance.

• Deep understanding of psychoacoustics, listening science, and subjective evaluation methodologies (e.g., MUSHRA test) including statistical analysis.

• Hands-on experience with industry-standard tools such as Audio Precision APx, SoundCheck, ear simulators, and precision measurement microphones (e.g., from Brüel & Kjær, GRAS).

• Proficiency in Python and/or MATLAB for measurement automation, signal processing, data analysis, and visualization.

Bonus Points if You Have:

• Experience with active noise control, headphone hear-through, spatial audio, noise reduction, AI-based audio processing, and other advanced audio technologies.

• Experience applying AI and data-driven approaches to acoustic evaluation, listening-test analysis, perceptual modelling, or measurement automation.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively within and across teams.

• Self-motivated, proactive, and capable of driving projects with a high degree of ownership.

• Passion for audio quality, innovation, and continuous learning.

Things To Know:

• Occasional international travel to other HARMAN sites is required.

• Professional working proficiency in English is required for effective day-to-day communication with regional engineering teams.
